questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to ride a motorbike safely
The history of mass-produced motorcycles
Famous films about motorbikes
How women on motorbikes are shown in the media
questions.why: Neil says today they're looking at women and bikes, based on a study of the 'gendered motorcycle'.

questions.q: What do Sam's and Neil's first images of motorbikes have in common?
options: Both are about pizza delivery
Both show men on bikes
Both come from films
Both show very fast bikes
questions.why: Neil says in both cases they associated motorbikes with male figures.

questions.q: According to Esperanza Miyake, what happens when you ride a motorbike at high speed?
options: Gender and race stop being important
You feel more like a man
You enjoy the space inside the bike
You become more afraid
questions.why: She says it dissolves gender and race; 'all these things stop mattering'.

questions.q: How is riding a bike different from driving a car, according to Esperanza Miyake?
options: It is more comfortable on long journeys
It is slower and you see more scenery
You are completely part of the outside world
You can listen to music with headphones on
questions.why: She says on a bike there's no interiority; you're part of the exterior world.

questions.q: What do Sam and Neil say about the word 'interiority'?
options: They both use it all the time at work
It is a new slang word from social media
It is not a real word, just a made-up one
Neither of them had heard or used it before
questions.why: Sam says she'd never heard or used it, and Neil says 'Me neither.'

questions.q: What problem does Esperanza Miyake see with the 'empowered' female biker image?
options: It is often very sexualised
It is too rare
It shows women riding too slowly
It makes women look silly
questions.why: She says 'she's empowered but she's in a skintight catsuit'.

questions.q: What is the second type of female rider she describes?
options: A silly, giggly woman riding a small scooter
A woman who looks and acts very masculine
A woman who races motorbikes professionally
A woman riding on the back with her boyfriend
questions.why: She describes a rider 'who's been masculinised' and embodies a masculine style.

questions.q: What does Neil conclude about images of women and motorbikes?
options: They are mostly positive and show strong women
They have improved a lot in the last few years
There are few fully positive images in the media
They are exactly the same as the images of men
questions.why: He says there don't seem to be many really completely positive images in the media.
